name: Free Scale Drawing Geometry Lesson PowerPoint Template
description: Teach scale drawings with an editable comparison grid, a worked example, guided practice, and an exit ticket.
longDescription: Use this free geometry PowerPoint to help learners connect corresponding lengths and reason about scale factor. A cobalt drafting grid anchors the worked comparison, guided activity, and misconception check. All diagrams and labels are native PowerPoint objects.
cover: Read and make a scale drawing
A classroom exercise that connects grids, lengths, and scale factors.

story.title: Compare shape before comparing size
story.body: Ask students which features stayed the same when a drawing grew.
points: Explain why a taller outline may be distorted.
Use the same factor for every matching length.

story.title: Count the matching sides
story.body: Compare the editable unit grids below and describe what happened to each side.
points: Match the marked edge to its copy.
Count squares along the corresponding edge.
Use the same multiplier across the shape.

story.title: Use a ratio to explain the scale
story.body: Divide the copy length by the original length in the same units.
points: The copy is twice as long along the marked edge.

story.title: Draw an enlargement on a fresh grid
story.body: Choose a short original path and enlarge it using the same factor on both axes.
points: Circle a starting point on each grid.
Apply the factor to each horizontal and vertical move.
Tell a partner what stayed unchanged.

story.title: Model, pair up, then draw solo
story.body: Pause after each activity to check that students can explain their choice.
points: Think aloud while pairing corresponding sides.
Have partners compare their drawn copies.
Ask each learner to show a second length check.

story.title: Find a drawing that used different factors
story.body: Offer a stretched outline and ask learners to identify the error.
points: Locate each original side on the copy.
Compare the horizontal and vertical factors.
Adjust the drawing and explain the change.

story.title: Show how you know the copy is to scale
story.body: Ask each learner for a drawing and a brief proportional explanation.
points: Make an enlargement on the grid.
Mark lengths on two corresponding pairs.
Describe the common scale factor in words.
